wsdl:definitions.name: Core_Implementation_Service
wsdl:definitions.wsdl:documentation: Web service operations designed for getting base application system setup data out of a root tenant, and for loading that data into a new tenant. The Request_* operations get tenant data out. The Load_* operations load setup data into a tenant. The output from the request operations is also the input to the load operations; this means you can take the setup data from one tenant and load it into another tenant. There is an automated process in the system that enables an empty tenant to load its setup data in the proper order from *any* system that exposes all of the Request_* operations. The other system does not need to know anything about the order of loading; it simply needs to implement the Request_* operations in this web service. Most of the Load_* operations ignore duplicates; this means that they can be re-run and duplicate values will be ignored. Load_* operations that do not ignore duplicates declare this in their documentation.

xsd:annotation.xsd:documentation: Country ISO code. If the Country ISO code is specified, then this ISO code will be used to determine the Country Phone Code for (eliminate space between f and o) the phone. Pass this ISO code to distinguish between multiple countries sharing the same Country Phone Code. (For example, 1 is the Country Phone Code that is shared by USA, Canada, Dominican Republic, Bermuda, Jamaica, and Puerto Rico.)

ISO Code identifying the country where the naming rules for this name are defined. Workday provides the ability for a customer to specify an ISO Code at the country level. Each customer can also define various rules around names, required fields for names, labels for name fields at the Country level. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-3

wsdl:portType.name: Core_Implementation_ServicePort
wsdl:portType.wsdl:documentation: Web service operations designed for getting base application system setup data out of a root tenant, and for loading that data into a new tenant. The Request_* operations get tenant data out. The Load_* operations load setup data into a tenant. The output from the request operations is also the input to the load operations; this means you can take the setup data from one tenant and load it into another tenant. There is an automated process in the system that enables an empty tenant to load its setup data in the proper order from *any* system that exposes all of the Request_* operations. The other system does not need to know anything about the order of loading; it simply needs to implement the Request_* operations in this web service. Most of the Load_* operations ignore duplicates; this means that they can be re-run and duplicate values will be ignored. Load_* operations that do not ignore duplicates declare this in their documentation.

wsdl:operation.name: Put_Location
wsdl:operation.wsdl:documentation: Adds or updates a location. Location addresses, usages, email addresses, phone numbers, time profile data, location attributes, location superior and location hierarchies can also be added and updated with this operation. The effective date must be blank for new locations to be consistent with the new locations created in the UI. The effective date applies to these fields: 1) Location Name 2) Inactive 3) Location Hierarchy Reference. If the Location Hierarchy Reference field is left blank for an existing location, the location will be removed from the location hierarchies it's included in. If these fields are left blank, any existing values will be removed: 1) Altitude 2) Latitude 3) Longitude 4) Trade Name 5) Worksite Identification Code 6) Locale 7) User Language 8) Location Attribute 9) Location Type 10) Time Profile 11) Time Zone 12) Superior Location. The Allow Duplicate Coordinates field enables you to provide duplicate location coordinates for latitude, longitude, and altitude and you can set the field to False to prevent duplicate location coordinates. You must also set the Allow Duplicate Coordinates field to Yes for existing locations when you want to update them. The Do Not Replace Business Site And Location Details field controls whether business site and location details will be replaced. If you set this field to True only these fields will be updated: 1) Location Type 2) Location Attribute 3) Superior Location 4) Time Profile 5) Locale 6) User Language 7) Time Zone 8) Currency 9) Trade Name 10) Worksite 11) Location Hierarchy Reference.Yes

wsdl:operation.name: Put_Workteam
wsdl:operation.wsdl:documentation:
This operation adds or deletes workteam members, or updates workteam members' membership status. Each membership status change is effective dated in order to capture membership status history. Each effective-dated membership status change is referred to as a snapshot.
When a workteam member is deleted, it is as if they were never a member and their entire membership status history is also deleted. If you want to retain membership status history after a member departs, Workday recommends that you change the member's status to Inactive instead.
When a worker does not exist as a workteam member as of the specified effective date, they are added as a member with the specified effective date and membership status. When a worker does exist as a workteam member as of the specified effective date, the operation updates their membership status. You can correct a membership status by using the same effective date as an existing membership status snapshot or correct the membership status to an earlier effective date by specifying the desired effective date and the same membership status as the next effective-dated snapshot.
Example: Membership status is Passive with effective date December 1, 2018. If you specify November 15, 2018 as the effective date and membership status as Passive, the system will change the effective date on the December 1, 2018 snapshot to November 15, 2018. If a workteam member is added too early, you can either delete the member entirely and add them again, or correct the membership status of the first snapshot to be Inactive and then add a new snapshot with the correct effective date and a membership status of Active or Passive.Not Applicable
